title: Arriving in Xi'an
summary: From complete beginner to chasing a craft I actually care about
markdown:
Hi — I'm a developer with about three years of experience. For a long time the path felt smooth: from someone who barely wrote code to someone who could ship things. Then, in June this year, I moved to Xi'an full of hope for what came next. Turns out the hard part was only beginning.

I interviewed at a lot of companies and got nowhere. Either my fundamentals weren't solid enough, so the offers couldn't match what I needed, or I never heard back at all. That sunk me for days. I kept replaying it: at my last job I could build web apps and mobile apps, pick up new tools quickly — so why couldn't I land a single offer here? The disappointment was hard to put into words.

There's a line people love: "Behind every successful man is a great woman." I believe it now. At my lowest point, my girlfriend Huihui kept talking me through it. She reminded me that letting go is sometimes how you make room to gain something, and that life swings both ways. What I needed wasn't another interview grind — it was to go back and fill in the basics, to understand programming through first principles. Time to learn again. Really learn. Sit with the craft. Embrace it.

So thank you to the interviewers who said no — you forced me to look at myself honestly. And thank you, Huihui, for holding the line when I couldn't.

From here on, I'll use this blog to track what I'm learning and how I'm growing. If something I write helps another developer who's been through a similar stretch, good. And if the act of writing pushes me deeper into the work, even better.

Time to start over — and chase the craft properly.
